subject: Civil Engineering
title: Drill and Blast Method
description: A 60-second lesson on Drill and Blast Method.

hook.text: Before TBMs existed, tunnels were blasted through rock — one explosion at a time.

buildup.text: Drill rigs bore precise holes into the rock face in a planned pattern.

discovery.text: Explosives are loaded, wired, and detonated in sequence — shaping the blast to break rock cleanly.

twist.text: Smooth blasting uses lighter charges at the perimeter — leaving a clean tunnel profile.

climax.text: Drill and blast is still preferred for short tunnels or irregular shapes — TBMs aren't always best.

punchline.text: Sometimes the best tool for rock is still controlled explosions.

quiz.question: When is drill and blast preferred over TBMs?
options: When the tunnel is very long and straight through soft clay
For short tunnels or irregular shapes where a TBM isn't cost-effective
When the tunnel must be built without any vibrations or noise

details.summary: Drill-and-blast tunneling excavates rock by drilling arrays of holes into the tunnel face, loading them with explosives, and detonating in precise sequences that break rock while controlling vibration and overbreak.
details.whyItMatters: Drill-and-blast is versatile and can handle any rock condition, cross-section shape, or tunnel size without the enormous capital cost of a TBM. It remains essential for short tunnels and variable conditions.
takeaways: Blast holes are drilled in precise patterns that control the shape of excavation
Detonation sequences progress from center outward to create a free face for breakage
Modern electronic detonators control timing to millisecond precision for vibration control

faq.question: How do engineers control vibration from tunnel blasting in urban areas?
faq.answer: Electronic detonators fire charges in precise millisecond sequences so only small amounts of explosive detonate simultaneously, reducing peak ground vibration. Perimeter holes use lighter charges to minimize overbreak.

faq.question: When is drill-and-blast preferred over a tunnel boring machine?
faq.answer: Drill-and-blast is preferred for short tunnels where TBM mobilization cost is unjustified, for non-circular cross-sections, extremely hard rock, highly variable ground conditions along the alignment, and large caverns where TBMs cannot operate. It offers flexibility that rigid TBMs cannot.
